sources: CCSDS 502.0-B-3 7.5.10: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.d->d][Z] or YYYY-DDDThh:mm:ss[.d->d][Z]; all fields with leading zeros; Z optional
iso: the instant each valid string denotes, as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.ffffff' UTC; a parse_epoch hook is compared with it within 2 us (D-119)

valid.note: CCSDS annex G example, day-of-year form
leap second: ss = 60 permitted (7.5.10 NOTE); a datetime cannot carry second 60, so the instant one second earlier (iso) or the next midnight (iso_alternatives) is accepted

invalid.reason: TLE epoch field, not an OMM epoch
only 'Z' is permitted as time-code terminator in 7.5.10 (the XSD pattern is more permissive)

parser_hazard: A parser hard-coded to '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f' (for example python-sgp4's sgp4.omm.initialize) rejects five of the valid strings above.
